schema: RB gloss overrides (Regula Benedicti). Keyed by the exact lexicon key (lowercase printed form). Each value is an `edited` card the reader shows on click: { lemma?, pos?, gloss, note? }. Where `lemma`/`pos` are omitted the entry keeps Whitaker's. Notes cite the Rule by chapter (Prologus, RB 1–73). This is a STARTER set — refine glosses against a critical text before treating them as final.

humilitas.gloss: humility — the ladder of twelve degrees by which the monk ascends to charity.
humilitas.note: RB 7 is the Rule's long chapter on humility; Bernard's De gradibus later rereads this same ladder.

humilitatis.note: 'Primus itaque humilitatis gradus' (RB 7). The degrees are to be climbed, not counted.

humilitatem.gloss: humility (acc.) — the height reached by the ladder.
humilitatem.note: RB 7: the monk who has climbed the degrees arrives at the love of God which casts out fear.

humilitate.gloss: by/in humility — the way of ascent (vs. pride's descent).
humilitate.note: RB 7: 'exaltatione descendere et humilitate ascendere' — one goes down by pride and up by humility.

superbia.gloss: pride — exaltation of self; the descent opposed to humility.
superbia.note: RB 7 opens: every exaltation is a kind of pride. The abbot must watch for pride in office (RB 64–65).

oboedientia.gloss: obedience — the first degree of humility; without delay, as if commanded by God.
oboedientia.note: RB 5: 'Primus humilitatis gradus est oboedientia sine mora.' Late spelling with -oe- (classical obedientia).

oboedientiae.gloss: of obedience — the labour by which one returns to God.
oboedientiae.note: Prologus: 'per oboedientiae laborem redeas'; RB 71 extends it brother to brother.

oboedientiam.note: See 'oboedientia'. Profession promises stabilitas, conversatio morum, and oboedientia (RB 58).

oboedire.gloss: to obey — to hear and do, as hearing the Lord in the superior.
oboedire.note: RB 5 cites 'Qui vos audit me audit'. Late -oe- spelling.

oboediens.gloss: obedient — subject even unto death, after Christ.
oboediens.note: RB 7, third degree: 'Factus oboediens usque ad mortem'.

inoboedientiae.gloss: disobedience — the sloth by which one went away from God.

abbas.gloss: abbot — holds the place of Christ in the monastery; more to serve than to rule.
abbas.note: RB 2: 'Christi enim agere vices in monasterio creditur'. RB 64: 'prodesse magis quam praeesse'.

abbate.note: See 'abbas'. Cenobites live 'sub regula vel abbate' (RB 1).

regula.gloss: the Rule — this 'least rule for beginners', not a measuring-rod.
regula.note: Whitaker lists the carpenter's ruler first. In RB, regula is the monastic rule (RB 3, 73).

regulam.note: RB 73: 'hanc minimam inchoationis regulam' — this least rule written for a beginning.

regulari.gloss: of the Rule — regular discipline, not 'bar-shaped'.
regulari.note: Whitaker's first sense is metal bars. In RB, 'disciplina regularis' is the Rule's correction (RB 23–30).

disciplina.gloss: discipline — the Rule's training and correction, not mere schooling.
disciplina.note: RB 2: one measure of disciplina according to merit. The degrees of humility are also 'gradus … disciplinae' (RB 7).

monasterium.gloss: monastery — the workshop of the spiritual art, with stability in the community.
monasterium.note: RB 4: 'Officina vero … claustra sunt monasterii et stabilitas in congregatione'.

conversationis.gloss: of (monastic) way of life — conversatio morum, not mere 'conversation'.
conversationis.note: RB 58 profession: stabilitas, conversatio morum, oboedientia. In RB conversatio is the lived monastic manner.

conversatione.gloss: by/in the monastic way of life.

stabilitas.gloss: stability — remaining in the community; a vow of profession.
stabilitas.note: RB 4 workshop: 'stabilitas in congregatione'. Promised at profession (RB 58).

caritas.gloss: charity — the love of God that crowns the twelve degrees and casts out fear.
caritas.note: RB 7 close: 'ad caritatem Dei … quae perfecta foris mittit timorem' (1 Jn 4:18).

gradus.gloss: degree, step — one rung of RB 7's twelve-degree ladder of humility.
gradus.note: Not a generic 'position'. RB 7 inserts 'diversos gradus humilitatis vel disciplinae' into Jacob's ladder.

gradibus.gloss: degrees, steps — the rungs of the humility ladder.

scala.gloss: ladder — Jacob's ladder, the monk's life set up toward heaven.
scala.note: RB 7: 'scala illa … quae in somnio Iacob apparuit'. Its two sides are body and soul.

scola.gloss: school — the 'school of the Lord's service' (dominici scola servitii).
scola.note: Prologus. Late spelling without h (classical schola). Benedict's image for the monastery.

oratorium.gloss: oratory — the monastic chapel, not an orator's hall.
oratorium.note: Whitaker reads 'orator'. In RB the oratorium is the place of the Work of God (RB 7, 19, 52).

novicius.gloss: novice — one on trial before profession.

coenobitarum.gloss: cenobites — monks living under a rule and an abbot; the strongest kind.
coenobitarum.note: RB 1: first of four kinds of monks. From κοινόβιον, common life.

anachoritarum.gloss: anchorites, hermits — trained in community, then fighting alone.
anachoritarum.note: RB 1: the second kind, not beginners but proven in the monastery.

sarabaitarum.gloss: Sarabaites — monks with no rule or shepherd; a most vile kind.
sarabaitarum.note: RB 1. Cassian's third kind; Whitaker has no card.

sarabaitis.note: RB 1: the gyrovagues are worse than the Sarabaites.

girovagum.gloss: gyrovague, landloper — the fourth kind: always wandering, never stable.
girovagum.note: RB 1. Verheyen: 'Landlopers'. Whitaker has no card.

praepositus.gloss: prior / provost — an officer set over others, under the abbot.
praepositus.note: Whitaker's verb 'place in front' first. In RB the praepositus is a dangerous second-in-command (RB 65).

cellararius.gloss: cellarer — steward of the monastery's goods, like a father to the community.
cellararius.note: RB 31. Treat vessels as sacred altar vessels. Whitaker sometimes splits the compound.

silentium.gloss: silence — especially at night and at table; the Rule of taciturnitas.
silentium.note: RB 6, 38, 42. Whitaker's first sense is the verb 'be silent'.

taciturnitatem.gloss: restraint in speech — keeping silence until asked.
taciturnitatem.note: RB 6 and RB 7 ninth degree. Stronger than mere quiet: a discipline of the tongue.

excommunicationis.gloss: excommunication — exclusion from the common table and oratory for faults.
excommunicationis.note: RB 23–30. Graded: from meals, then from oratory; not the later canonical penalty only.

claustra.gloss: enclosure — the monastery precinct as workshop of the spiritual art.
claustra.note: RB 4: 'claustra sunt monasterii'. Not merely a door-bolt.

hospitum.gloss: of guests — strangers received as Christ.
hospitum.note: RB 53: 'Omnes supervenientes hospites tamquam Christus suscipiantur'.

antefana.gloss: antiphon — the refrain sung with a psalm (late spelling of antiphona).
antefana.note: RB 9–17. Whitaker parses 'ante-' as a prefix. Traditional monastic Latin writes antefana.

diabulum.gloss: the devil — late spelling with u (classical diabolus).
diabulum.note: Prologus, RB 1. The traditional text keeps diabulum.

omnimo.gloss: altogether, entirely — late spelling of omnino.
omnimo.note: Frequent in this text (RB 7, 43, …). Whitaker misses the form.

obsculta.gloss: listen! — the Rule's first word; late for ausculta.
obsculta.note: Prologus: 'Obsculta, o fili, praecepta magistri'. The traditional opening; some MSS ausculta.

conple.gloss: fulfil, complete — late spelling without m (classical compleo).
conple.note: Prologus: 'efficaciter conple'. Compline in this text is likewise conpletorios.

ebdomada.gloss: week — a week's turn of service (from ἑβδομάς).
ebdomada.note: RB 38: the weekly reader. Whitaker has no card for this form.

ebdomadarii.note: RB 35, 38: kitchen and table servers of the week.

ebdomadarius.gloss: weekly server — the brother on this week's duty.

quirie.gloss: Kyrie (eleison) — 'Lord, have mercy', the litany of the hours.
quirie.note: RB 9, 17. Spelled Quirie in this text.

pedules.gloss: socks / foot-wrappings — part of the monk's clothing issue.
pedules.note: RB 55, with caligae (shoes). Whitaker has no card.

femolaria.gloss: drawers, breeches — extra garments issued for the road.
femolaria.note: RB 55: taken from the wardrobe for a journey and returned washed. Late for femoralia.

hospis.gloss: guest / stranger — received as Christ ('I was a stranger').
hospis.note: RB 53 quotes Mt 25: 'Hospis fui et suscepistis me'. Form hospis for hospes.

guilae.gloss: of the gullet / gluttony — late spelling of gulae.
guilae.note: RB 1: gyrovagues serve 'guilae inlecebris', the enticements of the throat.

inoboetientibus.gloss: to the disobedient — source slip for inoboedientibus.
inoboetientibus.note: RB 2. A transcription error in latin.md (extra t).

delinquentiump.gloss: of those who offend — source slip for delinquentium.
delinquentiump.note: RB 2: 'peccata delinquentium'. Trailing p in latin.md.

humulitatis.gloss: of humility — source slip for humilitatis.
humulitatis.note: RB 7 §8 (fourth degree). u for i in this text.

angarizati.gloss: impressed, compelled (to go a mile) — of Mt 5:41.
angarizati.note: RB 7, fourth degree. Greek ἀγγαρεύω via the Gospel.

multoloquio.gloss: in much speaking — late for multiloquio.
multoloquio.note: RB 7, ninth degree: 'in multoloquio non effugitur peccatum'.

centisemus.gloss: the hundredth — source slip for centesimus.

benectiones.gloss: Benedictions — the Canticle of the Three Children (Dan 3), not a slip for 'blessings' only.
benectiones.note: RB 12, Sunday Lauds: Benectiones et Laudes. Traditional office name; spelling lacks di.

directanei.gloss: said straight through — psalms without antiphons.

contagiet.gloss: infect, spread contagion — lest one sick sheep infect the flock.

stirpator.gloss: a waster, squanderer (of the monastery's substance).
stirpator.note: RB 31: the cellarer must not be 'prodigus … et stirpator substantiae monasterii'.

tyfo.gloss: arrogant puff / conceit (τῦφος) — pride in giving out the ration.
tyfo.note: RB 31: offer the appointed portion 'sine aliquo tyfo vel mora'.

petanda.gloss: things to be asked for — gerundive, what may be requested.
petanda.note: RB 31: 'petantur quae petanda sunt' at the proper hours.

musitatio.gloss: whispering, murmuring — no voice at table but the reader's.
musitatio.note: RB 38: 'nullus musitatio vel vox nisi solius legentis'.

indigeries.gloss: overloading, excess of food — what must never steal upon the monk.
indigeries.note: RB 39, citing Lk 21:34 on crapula. Not classical; Whitaker misses it.

eptaticum.gloss: the Heptateuch — Genesis–Judges; not to be read at night to weak minds.
eptaticum.note: RB 42. Spelled Eptaticum in this text.

signus.gloss: signal, bell — the sound that calls to the Work of God.
signus.note: RB 43: 'mox auditus fuerit signus'. Form in -us for signum.

ingatur.gloss: be joined — source slip for iungatur ('let a brother not join another').
ingatur.note: RB 48: 'Neque frater ad fratrem ingatur horis inconpetentibus'.

safirae.gloss: Sapphira — with Ananias, struck dead for fraud over property (Acts 5).
safirae.note: RB 57: craftsmen selling the monastery's work must remember Ananias and Sapphira.

inridit.gloss: he mocks — the novice who later breaks his promise mocks the one he vowed to.
inridit.note: RB 58. Form inridit for irridet / inridet.

samuhel.gloss: Samuel — the boy who judged elders; rank is not by age.
samuhel.note: RB 63: 'Samuhel et Danihel pueri presbyteros iudicaverunt'.

gerges.gloss: flocks — source slip for greges (Jacob: if I overdrive my flocks they will die).
gerges.note: RB 64, citing Gen 33:13 on the abbot's discretion.

sandala.gloss: scandals — source slip for scandala, grave scandals from appointing a prior.

inpossibilitatis.gloss: of impossibility — reasons why a command exceeds one's strength.

timor.gloss: fear — the 1st degree of humility: the fear of God ever before the eyes.
timor.note: RB 7: 'Primus ... humilitatis gradus est, si timorem Dei sibi ante oculos semper ponens'; the monk thinks God sees every thought.

voluntas.gloss: will — the 2nd degree of humility is not to love one's own will.
voluntas.note: RB 7: 'Secundus humilitatis gradus est, si propriam quis non amans voluntatem ...'; 'Voluntas habet poenam et necessitas parit coronam.'

voluntatem.note: See 'voluntas'. 'Non veni facere voluntatem meam, sed eius qui me misit' (Jn 6:38).

patientia.gloss: patience — the 4th degree of humility: silently enduring injuries.
patientia.note: RB 7: 'Quartus ... gradus est, si in ipsa oboedientia duris et contrariis rebus ... tacite conscientia patientiam amplectatur.' Whitaker parses the form as the verb patior.

confessionem.gloss: confession — the 5th degree: laying bare evil thoughts and secret sins to the abbot.
confessionem.note: RB 7: 'Quintus ... gradus est, si omnes cogitationes malas ... per humilem confessionem abbatem non celaverit suum.'

vilitate.gloss: in lowliness, abasement — the 6th degree: content with every lowliness.
vilitate.note: RB 7: 'Sextus ... gradus est, si omni vilitate vel extremitate contentus sit monachus.'

operarium.gloss: a lowly workman — the 6th degree: each counts himself a worthless labourer.
operarium.note: RB 7: 'velut operarium malum se iudicet et indignum'.

viliorem.gloss: lower, more worthless — the 7th degree: counting oneself beneath all.
viliorem.note: RB 7: 'Septimus ... gradus est: si omnibus se inferiorem et viliorem ... pronuntiet'. Whitaker yields no lemma for this comparative.

inferiorem.gloss: lower (acc.) — the 7th degree: deeming oneself the least.

risu.gloss: laughter — the 10th degree of humility avoids readiness to laugh.
risu.note: RB 7: 'Decimus ... gradus est, si non sit facilis ac promptus in risu'; 'Stultus in risu exaltat vocem suam' (Sir 21:23). Whitaker parses the form as the verb rideo.
